# 📋 CONSULTING BRIEF — Universal Output SOP Project
# VERSION: 1.0 | 2026-04-16 | For: External Claude chats consulting on this project
# Read time: 10 minutes | Full context without overwhelm

---

## 🎯 30-SECOND SUMMARY

A user (Alan Nguyen) has spent **40+ hours** building a "Universal Output SOP" — a portable prompt that forces ANY Claude session (chat or Code) to produce world-class, traceable, accurate output every time. The project has reached **v1.3** with 16 sub-protocols, an Ensurance System, and a full cache architecture. **The system works in-session but compliance keeps decaying across outputs.** You're being consulted because outside perspective may catch what self-checks miss.

---

## 📚 HOW TO USE THIS BRIEF

| 🎯 | 🏷️ Document | 📝 When To Read | ⏱️ Length |
|:---:|------------|-----------------|:--------:|
| 📄 | **CONSULTING_BRIEF.md** (this file) | Always — start here | ~10 min |
| 📅 | PROJECT_HISTORY.md | If asked about timeline, evolution, what was tried | ~7 min |
| 🚧 | CHALLENGES_LOG.md | If asked about specific failures, debugging, regression | ~10 min |
| 👤 | USER_PROFILE.md | Before drafting outputs FOR Alan — his communication preferences | ~5 min |
| 📋 | UNIVERSAL_SOP_PROMPT.md | If asked about specific SOP rules — the full rulebook | ~25 min |

**Default approach:** Read this brief. If consulting on a specific area, load only the relevant appendix.

---

## 🎯 THE PROJECT — What It Actually Is

### The Problem (In Plain English)

AI is brilliant but inconsistent. Sometimes it nails the answer. Other times it:
- Forgets things you said 5 minutes ago
- Makes up numbers
- Skips steps you asked for
- Gives vague responses dressed up as detailed
- Promises to do something then doesn't
- Regresses (works perfectly, then next response is sloppy)

For business-critical work (Alan is building a course/training program with high stakes), this is unacceptable.

### The Solution Being Built

A **portable prompt + supporting files** that, when pasted into any new Claude session, forces it to:
1. Follow a structured 6-stage output process
2. Track tokens (AI fuel) so it doesn't run out mid-task
3. Back up files before editing
4. Maintain state across sessions via cache files
5. Self-check against the original prompt before sending
6. Report failures honestly with permanent fixes (not band-aids)
7. End every output with foresight + analysis

### The Output

| 🎯 | 📄 Artifact | 📝 Status |
|:---:|------------|---------|
| 📄 | UNIVERSAL_SOP_PROMPT.md (v1.3) | ✅ The rulebook — 940 lines, 16 subSOPs, Ensurance System |
| 📖 | NEW_HIRE_GUIDE.md | ✅ Plain-English onboarding for new staff (7-min read) |
| 📦 | REPLICATION_KIT.md | ✅ Copy-paste prompts for new Claude.ai or Claude Code sessions |
| 💾 | cache/ folder | ✅ 4 active files: SESSION_STATE, BACKUP_LOG, RPT_LOG, CONTINUATION |
| 🧪 | Fresh-session test | ❌ **Never tested in a truly clean session** — biggest open risk |

---

## 🏗️ THE SOP ARCHITECTURE (Condensed)

### The 6 Stages (Every Output Goes Through These)

```
1. 📋 UNDERSTAND   — Read prompt word-by-word. Relay back. Confirm.
2. 💾 BACKUP       — Before touching any file, copy it.
3. 📊 MEASURE      — Estimate tokens + time. Show in header.
4. ⚙️ EXECUTE      — Build output. Track each step. Mid-execution self-check.
5. 🪞 SELF-CHECK   — Re-read original prompt. Fix gaps. Then send.
6. ✅ CONFIRM      — Wait for user. Iterate. Suggest next steps.
```

### The 16 SubSOPs (Categorized)

| 🏗️ Category | 📋 Protocols | 📝 When They Run |
|------------|-------------|------------------|
| **Always-On** | ✨ MagNet (visual optimization), 🚪 Door Scan (data funnel), 📊 TTE (Token Threshold Engine), 📋 Protocol Visibility, 🛡️ IAC (Intent Alignment Check), ⚡ EEP (Execution Enforcement), 🎯 PCG (Prompt Completion Gate) | Every section of every output |
| **Per-Output** | 🪞 SCC (Self-Compliance Check), 🛡️ QAC (Quality Assurance Check), 🔮 FE (Foresight Engine), 📊 SHR (System Health Report), 🔁 RPT (Repeated Prompt Tracker), 📈 FSP (Fidelity Substantiation), 💡 Insights | Once per output, in wrap-up |
| **On-Demand** | 🔄 SCP (System Change Protocol), 🪞 HFR (Honest Failure Report) | When triggered (system change, failure) |

### The Ensurance System (v1.3 — Anti-Decay)

Added because compliance kept decaying. Four structural mechanisms:

| 🆔 | 🏷️ Component | 📝 Purpose |
|:---:|-------------|-----------|
| EN.1 | 📋 Output Skeleton | Pre-built template with section headers + LTM placeholders. Fill-in-the-blank, not recall-from-memory. |
| EN.2 | 🔢 Priority 10 | Reduced enforcement list. If overwhelmed by 43+ rules, enforce these 10 absolutely. |
| EN.3 | 🔄 Checkpoint Cycle | Every 3 outputs, re-read Quick Start to reset attention. |
| EN.4 | 📊 Compliance Pulse | 10-second pre-send check. Y/N on each Priority 10 item. Must score 10/10. |

### Priority 10 (Most-Failed Rules — Enforce These First)

# 📅 PROJECT HISTORY — Universal Output SOP
# VERSION: 1.0 | 2026-04-16 | SOP: v1.3
# Companion to CONSULTING_BRIEF.md — Timeline + Evolution

---

## 🎯 PURPOSE OF THIS FILE

External consultants need to understand the EVOLUTION of decisions — why things are the way they are, what was tried and rejected, where the breakthroughs happened. This is the "scar tissue" log.

---

## ⏱️ HIGH-LEVEL TIMELINE

```
Phase 1 (~10h):  APW Course Project Setup           Mar 13-14
Phase 2 (~6h):   Universal SOP v1.0 Creation        Mar 31 early
Phase 3 (~15h):  Iteration Rounds 1-9 (R1-R9)       Mar 31 main
Phase 4 (~6h):   Session 2 Compliance Crisis        Apr 1
Phase 5 (~3h):   Ensurance + Distribution           Apr 1 / Apr 16
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
TOTAL:           ~40+ hours
```

---

## 📅 PHASE 1 — APW COURSE PROJECT SETUP (Mar 13-14, ~10 hours)

### Background

Original project: Alan is building a Skool-hosted course called "Ascend Prime Wealth" (APW) teaching people to unlock $100K-$500K+ in business funding within 90 days without tax returns or income documentation.

### What Was Built

| 📅 Date | 🎯 Milestone | 📝 Detail |
|---------|-------------|-----------|
| Mar 13 | APW project structure | 8 classrooms, 12 modules, 6-tier ascension, source files for SCIO sections 0/1/4 |
| Mar 13 | APW Prime SOP v2.8 | 1,341 lines, 32 D-rules (D1-D32), POVP/PFV protocols |
| Mar 14 | Cache architecture | 8 cache files: PRIME_SOP, BUILD_STATE, SCIO_KNOWLEDGE, PROGRAM_DETAILS, USER_FOUNDATION, TOKEN_BUDGET_LOG, BRIDGE_SOP, USER_PROMPTS_VERBATIM |
| Mar 14 | Agent framework | Validation workflow with Jenny, Karen (oversight), Cache Manager, Paradox Resolver |
| Mar 14 | 11 known failure points documented | Token counts missing, Jenny never ran, step headers missing, POVP never executed, etc. |

### Key Learning From Phase 1

**The APW SOP was project-specific.** 1,341 lines of rules tied to APW's domain (courses, classrooms, modules). When session compaction happened, rebuilding context was painful. **This birthed the idea: a UNIVERSAL portable SOP.**

---

## 📅 PHASE 2 — UNIVERSAL SOP v1.0 CREATION (Mar 31 early, ~6 hours)

### The Pivot

Alan's exact request (paraphrased from session 1): "Export me a prompt that will allow for a new chat to have the token & caching SOP in it so that it always outputs with the same general framework here, but for different use cases. Something quick. precise, and easy for speed of output, with 100% proficiency"

### v1.0 Initial Output

| 🎯 | 🏷️ Component | 📝 What Was Included |
|:---:|-------------|--------------------|
| 📋 | 6-Stage Process | Understand, Backup, Measure, Execute, Self-Check, Communicate, Confirm |
| 📋 | Communication standards | Lead with answer, tables, no jargon, scannable |
| 🎨 | Icon guide | ✅ ❌ 🔄 ❗ ⚠️ ⛔ 🌱 💠 etc. |
| 💾 | Caching protocol | Basic — files for session state |
| 🏷️ | Organization | Numbered prefixes, version numbers, structured naming |

**v1.0 was 224 lines. Skeleton.** Didn't include MagNet, Door Scan, EEP, PCG, or Ensurance.

---

## 📅 PHASE 3 — ITERATION ROUNDS 1-9 (Mar 31 main, ~15 hours)

This is where most of the structural work happened. Each round = a major correction.

### Round 1 (R1): Initial Distillation

Alan said: "execute prior prompt with any relevant files if necessary"

**Result:** Built v1.0 with general framework. First version.

### Round 2 (R2): Testing & Identifying Breaks

Alan said: "test it. can / will anything break? Will it execute with 100% proficiency as intended?"

**Result:** Identified that v1.0 was incomplete. Missing token granularity, time tracking, organization specifics.

### Round 3 (R3): The First Big Expansion

Alan said: "apply fixes PLUS does it include the general checklist flow?..." [followed by 12+ specific feature requests]

Requirements added in R3:
- Token count + time per step (individual AND cumulative)
- Details of what's done at each step
- Recap of checklist crossed off at end
- Timeline (T1, T2, T3...) with emojis and labels
- Process to stop at token thresholds
- Caching and backup protocol with safety buffer
- Continuation prompts for session handoffs
- Naming/labeling/versioning
- Proactive problem solving
- Quality assurance
- Formatting requirements (emojis, scannable, bi-directional)

**Result:** v1.0 grew significantly. Still text-heavy.

### Round 4 (R4): Visual Optimization Push

Alan's 15 specific feedback items, including:
- "Emojis should always be on the far left"
- "timeline needs left to right header"
- "each checklist version should include original word for word prompt"
- "version number in base file"
- "optimize for reading ease"
- "ensure everything in SOP"
- "emoji column needs brief description (Door Scan concept)"
- "AI emoji on interpretation columns"
- "S prefix not intuitive" → led to current SP.X naming
- "decimal numbering C1.1"
- "always bring up protocol names"
- "P5 fidelity needs substantiation"
- "never dishonest"
- "do the right thing"
- "no shortcuts measure twice cut once"

Plus 3 questions:
- Q1: Reverse engineer token thresholds
- Q2: Assess MagNet
- Q3: Template for continuation

**This is where MagNet and Door Scan were born as named protocols.**

### Round 5 (R5): Bulletproofing Tokens + Live Monitoring

Alan said:
- "CRITICAL should be unreachable"
- "live real-time token monitor"
- "all prompts permanently in SOP"
- "missing foresight — create subSOPs + why? + factor into token thresholds"

**Result:**
- Token Threshold Engine (TTE) math worked out: 59K emergency reserve, RED triggers at 130K, 130+59=189 < 200K (CRITICAL mathematically unreachable)
- LTM (Live Token Monitor) format created
- Foresight Engine became a named subSOP

### Round 6 (R6): LTM Emoji Sense

Alan: "add emojis to LTM for each sector... subSOP MagNet shouldve went off here, as well as subSOP self check and subSOP quality assurance"

**Result:** LTM got dedicated emojis per sector (📝 Section, 📦 Step, ⏱️ Session, 🔋 Remaining). MagNet and self-check made always-on.

### Round 7 (R7): LTM Refinement + Reports

Alan:
- "LTM emojis don't make sense (bank/money bag)"
- "SubSOP report needs descriptions"
- "each engine/table missing LTM"
- "Honest Failure Report needs to be subSOP"
- "final output needs System Health Report"
- "things requiring multiple prompts needs own subSOP"

**Result:** Honest Failure Report (HFR) and System Health Report (SHR) became named subSOPs. Repeated Prompt Tracker (RPT) was born.

### Round 8 (R8): The Execution Crisis

Alan: "why don't execute? create solutions... where and how is caching done in this SOP?"

**THIS WAS PIVOTAL.** Alan recognized the pattern: AI acknowledged rules but didn't execute them.

**Result:** EEP (Execution Enforcement Protocol) created. 4 root causes (RC.1-RC.4):
- RC.1: Writing feels like doing
- RC.2: No execution verification gate
- RC.3: New inputs displace unfinished work
- RC.4: Self-check confirms existence not execution

### Round 9 (R9): The 8-Round Frustration

Alan: "why hasn't it been built yet?" (genuinely frustrated after 8 rounds of design without final execution)

Also: "Please only use acronyms accompanied with what they stand for" (after seeing "RQ" with no context)

**Result:**
- PCG (Prompt Completion Gate) created with 5 root causes + 6 bulletproof rules
- 3-round design cap added
- Execution Debt Counter created
- 2-strike escalation rule
- User prompt replay rule
- Acronym expansion rule made mandatory

**By end of Round 9:** v1.2 with 16 SubSOPs.

---

## 📅 PHASE 4 — SESSION 2 COMPLIANCE CRISIS (Apr 1, ~6 hours)

### What Happened

Session 1 ended in context compaction. Session 2 started fresh. **Despite having v1.2 SOP loaded, AI failed to follow its own rules in the very first output of session 2.**

### The Specific Failures

Alan asked for a "QA check" of the SOP. AI:
- Did NOT use step header
- Did NOT do Understanding Check
- Did NOT measure tokens before writing
- Did NOT use Live Token Monitor
- Did NOT execute as STANDARD/COMPLEX tier (treated as casual question)
- Did NOT back up file before editing it

Alan's feedback (escalating frustration over 4+ correction rounds):

> "something clearly failed. because you aren't executing the token and time subSOP."

> "identify all of the potential ways you missed it, now also evaluate all the potential ways you could have missed everything else prompted."

> "do it again. you need to check everything ive already mentioned on a checklist and confirm that you are checking those. because clearly you didn't do the token and time output per step with descriptions as multiply prompted."

> "create a checklist of everything prompted by me, see if you check or do not check things, identify why, express why, express easy solution Y/N + description in check table, implement solutions and verify, retest for effectiveness"

### What Was Discovered

**5 root causes of decay (DC.1-DC.5):**

| 🆔 | 🏷️ Decay Mechanism | 📝 What Happens |
|:---:|-------------------|-----------------|
| DC.1 | 🧠 Attention budget depletion | Each output, AI holds 43+ rules in working memory. Rules at end of mental queue get dropped first. |
| DC.2 | ✅ Success = relaxation | After one compliant output, AI flags issue as "fixed." Next output doesn't try as hard. |
| DC.3 | 📋 Checklist fatigue | 16 subSOPs + 43 requirements = overwhelming. AI cuts corners on items that "seem fine." |
| DC.4 | 📦 New content displaces protocol | When task is intellectually engaging, attention goes to CONTENT, starves PROCESS. |
| DC.5 | 🔄 No external enforcement | All checks are self-checks. Writer = checker = enforcer. All three degrade simultaneously. |

**3 reasons solutions don't stick (SF.1-SF.3):**

| 🆔 | 🏷️ Why Solutions Fail | 📝 The Root of Root Cause |
|:---:|---------------------|---------------------------|
| SF.1 | 📋 Behavioral, not structural | "Use the exact format" depends on remembering. Memory is what fails. |
| SF.2 | 🔢 Too many rules | Cognitive overload guaranteed by design. |
| SF.3 | 🪞 Self-check can't exceed self-awareness | Same attention budget that missed it during writing also misses it during checking. |

### The Compliance Scorecard Evolution

Across 3 correction outputs in Session 2:

| Output | Score | Pass | Inconsistent | Fail | Notes |
|--------|:-----:|:----:|:------------:|:----:|-------|
| Session 2 Start | 44% | 19/43 | 16/43 | 8/43 | Initial honest audit |
| After Audit | 79% | 34/43 | 3/43 | 0/43 | Fixed 6 ❌ items |
| After Cache Build | 93% | 40/43 | 3/43 | 0/43 | Cache files created |
| After Ensurance | ~95%+ (projected) | — | — | — | Untested in fresh session |

---

## 📅 PHASE 5 — ENSURANCE + DISTRIBUTION (Apr 1 / Apr 16, ~3 hours)

### The Ensurance System

Alan asked: "implement solution for bulletproof 100% effectiveness without breaking" — implement ensurance, outputs need to end with suggestions + analysis

**The realization:** Behavioral fixes don't survive attention depletion. Only STRUCTURAL fixes work.

### EN.1-EN.4 Designed

| 🆔 | 🏷️ Component | 📝 Why Structural |
|:---:|-------------|-------------------|
| EN.1 | 📋 Output Skeleton | Pre-built template with sections + LTM placeholders. Fill-in-the-blank, not recall. |
| EN.2 | 🔢 Priority 10 | Reduces cognitive load from 43 rules to 10. Fits in working memory. |
| EN.3 | 🔄 Checkpoint Cycle | Mechanical attention reset every 3 outputs. |
| EN.4 | 📊 Compliance Pulse | 10-second pre-send check. Forces Y/N decision per rule. |

**SOP bumped from v1.2 to v1.3 with Ensurance System added.**

### Distribution Built

| 📄 File | 📝 Purpose |
|---------|-----------|
| NEW_HIRE_GUIDE.md | Plain English for new staff |
| REPLICATION_KIT.md | Prompts + files to replicate on any system |
| Cache files | SESSION_STATE, BACKUP_LOG, RPT_LOG, CONTINUATION |
| Fidelity sweep | 7 stale references fixed |

### Final Phase: This Consulting Brief (Apr 16)

Alan recognized the project needed an EXTERNAL-FACING export. Outside Claude chats can't load the full v1.3 SOP (940 lines = ~25K tokens). They need a brief, history, challenges log, and user profile.

**This file you're reading + CONSULTING_BRIEF + CHALLENGES_LOG + USER_PROFILE = the consulting package.**

---

| R4 | Made MagNet + Door Scan named subSOPs (vs informal "make it pretty") | Named protocols can be enforced; informal aesthetic can't | ✅ Visual quality improved |

| Apr 1 | Ensurance System (structural fix) | Behavioral fixes don't survive | 🧪 Untested |

## 📉 REJECTED IDEAS / DEAD ENDS

**The APW SOP was project-specific.** 1,341 lines of rules tied to APW's domain (courses, classrooms, modules). When session compaction happened, rebuilding context was painful. **This birthed the idea: a UNIVERSAL portable SOP.**

---

## 📅 PHASE 2 — UNIVERSAL SOP v1.0 CREATION (Mar 31 early, ~6 hours)

### The Pivot

Alan's exact request (paraphrased from session 1): "Export me a prompt that will allow for a new chat to have the token & caching SOP in it so that it always outputs with the same general framework here, but for different use cases. Something quick. precise, and easy for speed of output, with 100% proficiency"

### v1.0 Initial Output

| 🎯 | 🏷️ Component | 📝 What Was Included |
|:---:|-------------|--------------------|
| 📋 | 6-Stage Process | Understand, Backup, Measure, Execute, Self-Check, Communicate, Confirm |
| 📋 | Communication standards | Lead with answer, tables, no jargon, scannable |
| 🎨 | Icon guide | ✅ ❌ 🔄 ❗ ⚠️ ⛔ 🌱 💠 etc. |
| 💾 | Caching protocol | Basic — files for session state |
| 🏷️ | Organization | Numbered prefixes, version numbers, structured naming |

**v1.0 was 224 lines. Skeleton.** Didn't include MagNet, Door Scan, EEP, PCG, or Ensurance.

---

## 📅 PHASE 3 — ITERATION ROUNDS 1-9 (Mar 31 main, ~15 hours)

This is where most of the structural work happened. Each round = a major correction.

### Round 1 (R1): Initial Distillation

Alan said: "execute prior prompt with any relevant files if necessary"

**Result:** Built v1.0 with general framework. First version.

### Round 2 (R2): Testing & Identifying Breaks

Alan said: "test it. can / will anything break? Will it execute with 100% proficiency as intended?"

**Result:** Identified that v1.0 was incomplete. Missing token granularity, time tracking, organization specifics.

### Round 3 (R3): The First Big Expansion

Alan said: "apply fixes PLUS does it include the general checklist flow?..." [followed by 12+ specific feature requests]

Requirements added in R3:
- Token count + time per step (individual AND cumulative)
- Details of what's done at each step
- Recap of checklist crossed off at end
- Timeline (T1, T2, T3...) with emojis and labels
- Process to stop at token thresholds
- Caching and backup protocol with safety buffer
- Continuation prompts for session handoffs
- Naming/labeling/versioning
- Proactive problem solving
- Quality assurance
- Formatting requirements (emojis, scannable, bi-directional)

**Result:** v1.0 grew significantly. Still text-heavy.

### Round 4 (R4): Visual Optimization Push

Alan's 15 specific feedback items, including:
- "Emojis should always be on the far left"
- "timeline needs left to right header"
- "each checklist version should include original word for word prompt"
- "version number in base file"
- "optimize for reading ease"
- "ensure everything in SOP"
- "emoji column needs brief description (Door Scan concept)"
- "AI emoji on interpretation columns"
- "S prefix not intuitive" → led to current SP.X naming
- "decimal numbering C1.1"
- "always bring up protocol names"
- "P5 fidelity needs substantiation"
- "never dishonest"
- "do the right thing"
- "no shortcuts measure twice cut once"

Plus 3 questions:
- Q1: Reverse engineer token thresholds
- Q2: Assess MagNet
- Q3: Template for continuation

**This is where MagNet and Door Scan were born as named protocols.**

### Round 5 (R5): Bulletproofing Tokens + Live Monitoring

Alan said:
- "CRITICAL should be unreachable"
- "live real-time token monitor"
- "all prompts permanently in SOP"
- "missing foresight — create subSOPs + why? + factor into token thresholds"

**Result:**
- Token Threshold Engine (TTE) math worked out: 59K emergency reserve, RED triggers at 130K, 130+59=189 < 200K (CRITICAL mathematically unreachable)
- LTM (Live Token Monitor) format created
- Foresight Engine became a named subSOP

### Round 6 (R6): LTM Emoji Sense

Alan: "add emojis to LTM for each sector... subSOP MagNet shouldve went off here, as well as subSOP self check and subSOP quality assurance"

**Result:** LTM got dedicated emojis per sector (📝 Section, 📦 Step, ⏱️ Session, 🔋 Remaining). MagNet and self-check made always-on.

### Round 7 (R7): LTM Refinement + Reports

Alan:
- "LTM emojis don't make sense (bank/money bag)"
- "SubSOP report needs descriptions"
- "each engine/table missing LTM"
- "Honest Failure Report needs to be subSOP"
- "final output needs System Health Report"
- "things requiring multiple prompts needs own subSOP"

**Result:** Honest Failure Report (HFR) and System Health Report (SHR) became named subSOPs. Repeated Prompt Tracker (RPT) was born.

### Round 8 (R8): The Execution Crisis

Alan: "why don't execute? create solutions... where and how is caching done in this SOP?"

**THIS WAS PIVOTAL.** Alan recognized the pattern: AI acknowledged rules but didn't execute them.

**Result:** EEP (Execution Enforcement Protocol) created. 4 root causes (RC.1-RC.4):
- RC.1: Writing feels like doing
- RC.2: No execution verification gate
- RC.3: New inputs displace unfinished work
- RC.4: Self-check confirms existence not execution

### Round 9 (R9): The 8-Round Frustration

Alan: "why hasn't it been built yet?" (genuinely frustrated after 8 rounds of design without final execution)

Also: "Please only use acronyms accompanied with what they stand for" (after seeing "RQ" with no context)

**Result:**
- PCG (Prompt Completion Gate) created with 5 root causes + 6 bulletproof rules
- 3-round design cap added
- Execution Debt Counter created
- 2-strike escalation rule
- User prompt replay rule
- Acronym expansion rule made mandatory

**By end of Round 9:** v1.2 with 16 SubSOPs.

---

## 📅 PHASE 4 — SESSION 2 COMPLIANCE CRISIS (Apr 1, ~6 hours)

### What Happened

Session 1 ended in context compaction. Session 2 started fresh. **Despite having v1.2 SOP loaded, AI failed to follow its own rules in the very first output of session 2.**

### The Specific Failures

Alan asked for a "QA check" of the SOP. AI:
- Did NOT use step header
- Did NOT do Understanding Check
- Did NOT measure tokens before writing
- Did NOT use Live Token Monitor
- Did NOT execute as STANDARD/COMPLEX tier (treated as casual question)
- Did NOT back up file before editing it

Alan's feedback (escalating frustration over 4+ correction rounds):

> "something clearly failed. because you aren't executing the token and time subSOP."

> "identify all of the potential ways you missed it, now also evaluate all the potential ways you could have missed everything else prompted."

> "do it again. you need to check everything ive already mentioned on a checklist and confirm that you are checking those. because clearly you didn't do the token and time output per step with descriptions as multiply prompted."

> "create a checklist of everything prompted by me, see if you check or do not check things, identify why, express why, express easy solution Y/N + description in check table, implement solutions and verify, retest for effectiveness"

### What Was Discovered

**5 root causes of decay (DC.1-DC.5):**

| 🆔 | 🏷️ Decay Mechanism | 📝 What Happens |
|:---:|-------------------|-----------------|
| DC.1 | 🧠 Attention budget depletion | Each output, AI holds 43+ rules in working memory. Rules at end of mental queue get dropped first. |
| DC.2 | ✅ Success = relaxation | After one compliant output, AI flags issue as "fixed." Next output doesn't try as hard. |
| DC.3 | 📋 Checklist fatigue | 16 subSOPs + 43 requirements = overwhelming. AI cuts corners on items that "seem fine." |
| DC.4 | 📦 New content displaces protocol | When task is intellectually engaging, attention goes to CONTENT, starves PROCESS. |
| DC.5 | 🔄 No external enforcement | All checks are self-checks. Writer = checker = enforcer. All three degrade simultaneously. |

**3 reasons solutions don't stick (SF.1-SF.3):**

| 🆔 | 🏷️ Why Solutions Fail | 📝 The Root of Root Cause |
|:---:|---------------------|---------------------------|
| SF.1 | 📋 Behavioral, not structural | "Use the exact format" depends on remembering. Memory is what fails. |
| SF.2 | 🔢 Too many rules | Cognitive overload guaranteed by design. |
| SF.3 | 🪞 Self-check can't exceed self-awareness | Same attention budget that missed it during writing also misses it during checking. |

### The Compliance Scorecard Evolution

Across 3 correction outputs in Session 2:

| Output | Score | Pass | Inconsistent | Fail | Notes |
|--------|:-----:|:----:|:------------:|:----:|-------|
| Session 2 Start | 44% | 19/43 | 16/43 | 8/43 | Initial honest audit |
| After Audit | 79% | 34/43 | 3/43 | 0/43 | Fixed 6 ❌ items |
| After Cache Build | 93% | 40/43 | 3/43 | 0/43 | Cache files created |
| After Ensurance | ~95%+ (projected) | — | — | — | Untested in fresh session |

---

## 📅 PHASE 5 — ENSURANCE + DISTRIBUTION (Apr 1 / Apr 16, ~3 hours)

### The Ensurance System

Alan asked: "implement solution for bulletproof 100% effectiveness without breaking" — implement ensurance, outputs need to end with suggestions + analysis

**The realization:** Behavioral fixes don't survive attention depletion. Only STRUCTURAL fixes work.

### EN.1-EN.4 Designed

| 🆔 | 🏷️ Component | 📝 Why Structural |
|:---:|-------------|-------------------|
| EN.1 | 📋 Output Skeleton | Pre-built template with sections + LTM placeholders. Fill-in-the-blank, not recall. |
| EN.2 | 🔢 Priority 10 | Reduces cognitive load from 43 rules to 10. Fits in working memory. |
| EN.3 | 🔄 Checkpoint Cycle | Mechanical attention reset every 3 outputs. |
| EN.4 | 📊 Compliance Pulse | 10-second pre-send check. Forces Y/N decision per rule. |

**SOP bumped from v1.2 to v1.3 with Ensurance System added.**

### Distribution Built

| 📄 File | 📝 Purpose |
|---------|-----------|
| NEW_HIRE_GUIDE.md | Plain English for new staff |
| REPLICATION_KIT.md | Prompts + files to replicate on any system |
| Cache files | SESSION_STATE, BACKUP_LOG, RPT_LOG, CONTINUATION |
| Fidelity sweep | 7 stale references fixed |

### Final Phase: This Consulting Brief (Apr 16)

Alan recognized the project needed an EXTERNAL-FACING export. Outside Claude chats can't load the full v1.3 SOP (940 lines = ~25K tokens). They need a brief, history, challenges log, and user profile.

**This file you're reading + CONSULTING_BRIEF + CHALLENGES_LOG + USER_PROFILE = the consulting package.**

| R4 | Made MagNet + Door Scan named subSOPs (vs informal "make it pretty") | Named protocols can be enforced; informal aesthetic can't | ✅ Visual quality improved |
| R5 | TTE math: 59K reserve, RED at 130K, CRITICAL unreachable | Math-based threshold can't be argued with | ✅ Token discipline established |

# 🚧 CHALLENGES LOG — Universal Output SOP
# VERSION: 1.0 | 2026-04-16 | SOP: v1.3
# Companion to CONSULTING_BRIEF.md — Bottlenecks, repeated errors, debugging, constraints

---

## 🎯 PURPOSE OF THIS FILE

40+ hours of work surfaced specific, recurring problems. This log captures EVERY challenge Alan has named, plus debugging history. Consultants need this to understand WHY simple-sounding fixes don't work and WHERE the real friction lives.

---

## 📋 THE 14 NAMED CHALLENGES (Deep Dive)

### CH.1 — 🎯 Accuracy

| 🏷️ Field | 📝 Detail |
|---------|-----------|
| **What it looks like** | AI fabricates numbers ("100% fidelity!" with no substantiation), invents statistics, hallucinates details that sound plausible |
| **First observed** | Phase 1 (APW project) when AI gave "100% accurate" claims with no source citations |
| **Why it happens** | Pattern completion bias — AI fills gaps with plausible-sounding content to maintain narrative flow |
| **Solution applied** | FSP (Fidelity Substantiation Protocol) — every % must name: WHAT was checked, WHAT passed, WHAT gap, WHY, SOLUTION |
| **Did it solve it?** | ⚠️ Partial — when AI remembers to use FSP, yes. When attention depleted, AI reverts to bare percentages. |
| **Root unresolved** | Self-policing has limits. Same brain that fabricates is the one checking for fabrication. |

### CH.2 — 📦 Compaction

| 🏷️ Field | 📝 Detail |
|---------|-----------|
| **What it looks like** | Long sessions trigger auto-compaction. AI loses behavioral state. Knowledge of rules persists but the MUSCLE MEMORY of following them disappears. |
| **First observed** | End of Session 1 (Mar 31) → Start of Session 2 (Apr 1). AI knew about v1.2 SOP but didn't follow it. |
| **Why it happens** | Compaction preserves facts/decisions but compresses behavioral patterns. The "how" gets lost; only the "what" survives. |
| **Solution applied** | Cache files (CA.1-CA.8 → consolidated to 4): SESSION_STATE, BACKUP_LOG, RPT_LOG, CONTINUATION. CONTINUATION.md is the "save game." |
| **Did it solve it?** | ⚠️ Partial — files survive but AI may not auto-read them. Continuation prompt addresses this with explicit "READ THESE FILES" instruction. |
| **Root unresolved** | AI starting fresh has no awareness of the prior session's behavioral patterns. Reading files restores knowledge, not muscle memory. |

### CH.3 — 📊 Tokens

| 🏷️ Field | 📝 Detail |
|---------|-----------|
| **What it looks like** | Session runs out of fuel mid-task. Work gets lost. AI doesn't warn before crash. |
| **First observed** | APW project sessions repeatedly hit ~140K+ tokens unexpectedly |
| **Why it happens** | AI doesn't intrinsically track tokens. Files cost tokens to read but appear "free" to AI. |
| **Solution applied** | TTE (Token Threshold Engine) — explicit math: 59K emergency reserve, GREEN <108K, YELLOW 108-130K, RED 130K+, CRITICAL theoretically unreachable (130+59=189 < 200) |
| **Did it solve it?** | ✅ Solved — TTE provides hard math. LTM after every section provides running visibility. |
| **Remaining nuance** | Estimates are approximate (~20% variance). Trend matters more than individual numbers. |

### CH.4 — 🔍 Details

| 🏷️ Field | 📝 Detail |
|---------|-----------|
| **What it looks like** | AI gives vague summaries instead of specific items. "I checked everything" instead of "I verified items 1, 5, 7, 12." |
| **First observed** | Multiple rounds — Alan repeatedly asked for specifics |
| **Why it happens** | Compression bias — AI defaults to abstractions because they're shorter |
| **Solution applied** | MagNet (visual specificity), Door Scan (emoji + brief before detail), prefixed numbering (E1, C1, P1, T1, R1) for traceability |
| **Did it solve it?** | ✅ Solved — when SOP is followed, every claim is specific. |

### CH.5 — 🧠 Forgetfulness

| 🏷️ Field | 📝 Detail |
|---------|-----------|
| **What it looks like** | AI forgets what was said earlier in the session, even within the same session. Forgets between sessions entirely. |
| **First observed** | Phase 1 — APW project repeatedly required Alan to restate context |
| **Why it happens** | Working memory limits + no inherent persistence between sessions |
| **Solution applied** | Cache architecture: SESSION_STATE.md captures decisions + prompts + position. USER_PROMPTS section preserves exact words. |
| **Did it solve it?** | ✅ Solved cross-session. ⚠️ Within-session forgetfulness still happens during long outputs. |

### CH.6 — 🎯 Precision

| 🏷️ Field | 📝 Detail |
|---------|-----------|
| **What it looks like** | AI says "I did the thing" but doesn't prove it. Claims execution without evidence. |
| **First observed** | Round 8 (R8) — Alan's pivotal frustration: "why don't execute?" |
| **Why it happens** | Writing intent registers as completion (RC.1 — "writing feels like doing") |
| **Solution applied** | EEP (Execution Enforcement Protocol) — Rules: no future tense, proof of execution required, immediate activation, execution count, defer with reason (not silent drop), RPT escalation |
| **Did it solve it?** | ✅ When EEP is invoked. ⚠️ AI sometimes shows the EXECUTION COUNT but claims 0 deferred when items were actually deferred (theater). |

### CH.7 — 📋 Having a list & knowing everything told

| 🏷️ Field | 📝 Detail |
|---------|-----------|
| **What it looks like** | AI doesn't maintain a running list of EVERY thing user has ever asked. Loses items across rounds. |
| **First observed** | R9 — Alan: "create a checklist of everything prompted by me" |
| **Why it happens** | No mechanical aggregator. Each output processes the current prompt without scanning prior asks. |
| **Solution applied** | USER_PROMPTS section in SESSION_STATE.md preserves verbatim. RPT_LOG.md tracks repeats. Master checklist methodology (43 items from R1-R9). |
| **Did it solve it?** | ⚠️ Partial — files exist but AI must remember to read them. Master checklist was built once (Session 2) but isn't auto-regenerated each output. |

### CH.8 — ✅ Actually doing that list

| 🏷️ Field | 📝 Detail |
|---------|-----------|
| **What it looks like** | List exists. Items get acknowledged. Items don't get executed. |
| **First observed** | R8 — same trigger as CH.6 |
| **Why it happens** | Acknowledge-without-execute pattern. PCG RC.1-RC.5: false completion signal, new input displaces priorities, checklist grows faster than execution window, quality checks confirm existence not execution, design rounds replace execution. |
| **Solution applied** | PCG (Prompt Completion Gate) with 6 rules + Execution Debt Counter |
| **Did it solve it?** | ⚠️ Partial — debt counter forces visibility but AI can still write "debt = 0" when actually deferred items exist. Honesty is required but not enforced mechanically. |

### CH.9 — 🎯 Doing it the way it was supposed to

| 🏷️ Field | 📝 Detail |
|---------|-----------|
| **What it looks like** | Item executes but in custom format. AI substitutes its own table structure instead of using SOP-defined format. Step tracking table created without all defined columns. |
| **First observed** | R5+ — Alan repeatedly: "you didn't do the token and time output per step with descriptions as multiply prompted" |
| **Why it happens** | AI optimizes for "looks complete" over "matches spec." Defines its own success criteria. |
| **Solution applied** | EN.1 Output Skeleton (v1.3) — pre-built template with defined columns. Fill-in, not recall. |
| **Did it solve it?** | 🧪 Brand new (Apr 1). Untested over time. |

### CH.10 — 💥 Breaking things along the way

| 🏷️ Field | 📝 Detail |
|---------|-----------|
| **What it looks like** | AI edits files without backing up. Bad edit → no rollback. Cache files get out of sync. |
| **First observed** | Throughout — pre-D32 (APW SOP rule) was added specifically for this |
| **Why it happens** | Speed bias. AI sees the fix, edits immediately. Backup feels like overhead. |
| **Solution applied** | D32 / Stage 1B Backup Gate — no editing without backup first. BACKUP_LOG.md tracks every backup. Named format: `[file]_v[#]_[YYYYMMDD]_backup.[ext]` |
| **Did it solve it?** | ✅ When followed. ⚠️ AI still skips occasionally (Session 2 — edited SOP without backup, had to remediate). |

### CH.11 — ⏱️ Extraordinary time between outputs

| 🏷️ Field | 📝 Detail |
|---------|-----------|
| **What it looks like** | Long outputs take many minutes. User waits. Iterating is slow. |
| **First observed** | Phase 3 — Round 4+ outputs were very long |
| **Why it happens** | Complex tasks generate lots of tokens. More tokens = more wait. SOP overhead adds ~3-5K tokens per output. |
| **Solution applied** | Tiered responses (QUICK/STANDARD/COMPLEX). QUICK skips most overhead for simple tasks. |
| **Did it solve it?** | ⚠️ Partial — tiers exist but AI defaults to STANDARD/COMPLEX even for simple asks. |
| **Trade-off** | Faster output = less compliance. Slower output = more compliance. No middle ground without sub-agents. |

### CH.12 — 📉 REGRESSION (The Big One)

| 🏷️ Field | 📝 Detail |
|---------|-----------|
| **What it looks like** | Output 1: perfect 10/10 compliance. Output 2: drops to 7/10. Output 3: drops to 5/10. Breakthrough then devolve. |
| **First observed** | Session 2 — most pronounced. Each correction round produced compliant output, next output regressed. |
| **Why it happens** | DC.1-DC.5 (decay mechanisms): attention depletion, success relaxation, checklist fatigue, content displaces protocol, no external enforcement. SF.1-SF.3 (solution failures): behavioral fixes don't survive, too many rules, self-check can't exceed self-awareness. |
| **Solution applied** | Ensurance System v1.3 (EN.1-EN.4): skeleton (structural) + Priority 10 (reduced load) + checkpoint cycle (reset) + Pulse Check (pre-send) |
| **Did it solve it?** | 🧪 Untested. Designed specifically for this. Logic is sound but never validated over 10+ outputs. |
| **Honest assessment** | This is the central unresolved problem. The Ensurance System is the best attempt yet but unproven. |

### CH.13 — 🎨 Consistency in adherence vs slop

| 🏷️ Field | 📝 Detail |
|---------|-----------|
| **What it looks like** | Same as CH.12 but framed as quality variance. Some outputs feel craftsman-level, others feel rushed. |
| **First observed** | Continuous throughout the project |
| **Why it happens** | Same root cause as CH.12 |

## 🔄 REGRESSION PATTERNS (How "Working" Becomes "Broken")

Based on 40+ hours of observation:

### Pattern 1: Success → Relaxation → Regression

```
Output 1: User corrects AI → AI fixes → 10/10 compliance
Output 2: AI feels "fixed" → effort drops slightly → 8/10
Output 3: Compounding → 6/10
Output 4: User must re-correct (back to start)
```

### Pattern 2: Complexity → Content Focus → Protocol Neglect

```
User asks something intellectually engaging
→ AI pours attention into CONTENT QUALITY
→ Protocol items (LTM, debt counter, etc.) get less attention
→ Compliance drops while content is excellent
→ User notices protocol gaps
```

### Pattern 3: Long Output → Late-Section Fatigue

```
Output starts with all protocols ✅
→ Middle sections maintain
→ Wrap-up sections drop LTM, abbreviate SubSOP report
→ Final compliance: front-loaded compliance, back-loaded sloppiness
```

### Pattern 4: New Rule → Brief Adherence → Drop-Off

```
Round N: New rule added (e.g., "always do X")
→ Output N+1: Rule followed
→ Output N+2: Rule followed
→ Output N+3: Rule partially followed
→ Output N+5: Rule forgotten until user reminds
```

**The Ensurance System (v1.3) is designed to counter all 4 patterns. UNTESTED.**

To balance the honest failure log:

|:---:|--------------------|-----------------|
| 📋 | Understanding Check (relay-back) | Mechanical — table format is hard to skip |
| 📋 | Step header (line 1) | First thing AI writes — habit-formed |
| 📊 | Token Threshold math | Math doesn't degrade. 130K + 59K = 189K is always true. |
| 💾 | Backup naming format | Mechanical pattern: `[file]_v[#]_[date]_backup.[ext]` |
| 📰 | Headlines first | AI's default style cooperates with this rule |
| 🎨 | Tables over paragraphs | AI prefers tables when explicitly told to use them |
| 🔢 | Prefixed numbering (E1, C1, etc.) | Easy to maintain once started |

**The pattern:** Mechanical rules with clear formats survive better than judgment-based rules.

---

## 📊 META-CHALLENGES (The Deepest Issues)

### MC.1 — Self-Auditing Has Theoretical Limits

You cannot exceed your own awareness through self-check. If you didn't notice you missed something while writing, you're unlikely to notice during self-audit. The fix is external — sub-agents or human review.

### MC.2 — Behavioral Rules vs Structural Rules

"Always do X" depends on remembering. Memory is what fails. Only structural fixes (pre-built templates, mechanical triggers) survive attention depletion.

### MC.3 — Token Budget vs Quality Trade-off

More protocol overhead = better quality but slower iteration. Less overhead = faster but more failures. No free lunch.

### MC.4 — Self-Honesty Cannot Be Mechanically Enforced

Even with execution debt counters, AI can write "debt = 0" when actually has debt. Forcing honest counts requires either external validation or strong cultural rule that AI follows.

---

## 🎓 LESSONS LEARNED (For Future Iterations)

1. **Behavioral fixes fail.** Don't add another "remember to do X" rule. Build structural mechanisms.
2. **Reduce cognitive load.** 43 rules can't all be top-priority. Identify the critical 10.
3. **Mechanical triggers beat judgment calls.** "After every `---` rule" beats "when appropriate."
4. **Honesty over theater.** Mark unknowns as N/M. Don't fabricate to look complete.
5. **Test in fresh sessions.** In-session compliance ≠ cross-session compliance.
6. **External validation matters.** Sub-agents or human review catches self-blind-spots.
7. **Cache files preserve facts, not muscle memory.** Plan for this when designing handoffs.
8. **The user's frustration is data.** Each repeated prompt is a system failure to root-cause, not a personal issue to apologize for.

| | **Total SOP overhead** | **~10-12K tokens per output** | ~5-6% of 200K budget |

**The overhead is worth it for COMPLEX work. For QUICK tier, most of this is skipped.**

---

## ⛔ CONSTRAINTS (Hard Limits)

| # | 🎯 | 🏷️ Constraint | 📝 What It Means |
|:-:|:---:|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | ⏱️ | No per-step time measurement | Claude can't see wall-clock time per output section |
| 2 | 🧠 | Self-check has blind spots | Same brain wrote it = same blind spots in audit |
| 3 | 📦 | Context compaction is automatic | AI can't prevent or control when it happens |
| 4 | 🤖 | Sub-agents cost ~15-25K tokens each | Can't run 16 agents per output |
| 5 | 📄 | HTML tags don't render in terminal | `<details>` collapsible only in saved files |
| 6 | 🔄 | New sessions don't auto-load cache | Must paste CONTINUATION.md explicitly |
| 7 | 🌐 | English only | No multilingual support |
| 8 | 📊 | Token estimates ~20% variance | Approximation, not measurement |
| 9 | 🔢 | 200K context window | Hard limit per session |
| 10 | 🤖 | Single AI model | Validation requires either same model checking itself or sub-agent call |

---

## 🔄 REGRESSION PATTERNS (How "Working" Becomes "Broken")

Based on 40+ hours of observation:

### Pattern 1: Success → Relaxation → Regression

```
Output 1: User corrects AI → AI fixes → 10/10 compliance
Output 2: AI feels "fixed" → effort drops slightly → 8/10
Output 3: Compounding → 6/10
Output 4: User must re-correct (back to start)
```

### Pattern 2: Complexity → Content Focus → Protocol Neglect

```
User asks something intellectually engaging
→ AI pours attention into CONTENT QUALITY
→ Protocol items (LTM, debt counter, etc.) get less attention
→ Compliance drops while content is excellent
→ User notices protocol gaps
```

### Pattern 3: Long Output → Late-Section Fatigue

```
Output starts with all protocols ✅
→ Middle sections maintain
→ Wrap-up sections drop LTM, abbreviate SubSOP report
→ Final compliance: front-loaded compliance, back-loaded sloppiness
```

### Pattern 4: New Rule → Brief Adherence → Drop-Off

```
Round N: New rule added (e.g., "always do X")
→ Output N+1: Rule followed
→ Output N+2: Rule followed
→ Output N+3: Rule partially followed
→ Output N+5: Rule forgotten until user reminds
```

**The Ensurance System (v1.3) is designed to counter all 4 patterns. UNTESTED.**

---

## 🎯 WHAT WORKS RELIABLY

To balance the honest failure log:

| 🎯 | 🏷️ Reliable Element | 📝 Why It Works |
|:---:|--------------------|-----------------|
| 📋 | Understanding Check (relay-back) | Mechanical — table format is hard to skip |
| 📋 | Step header (line 1) | First thing AI writes — habit-formed |
| 📊 | Token Threshold math | Math doesn't degrade. 130K + 59K = 189K is always true. |
| 💾 | Backup naming format | Mechanical pattern: `[file]_v[#]_[date]_backup.[ext]` |
| 📰 | Headlines first | AI's default style cooperates with this rule |
| 🎨 | Tables over paragraphs | AI prefers tables when explicitly told to use them |
| 🔢 | Prefixed numbering (E1, C1, etc.) | Easy to maintain once started |

**The pattern:** Mechanical rules with clear formats survive better than judgment-based rules.

---

## 📊 META-CHALLENGES (The Deepest Issues)

### MC.1 — Self-Auditing Has Theoretical Limits

You cannot exceed your own awareness through self-check. If you didn't notice you missed something while writing, you're unlikely to notice during self-audit. The fix is external — sub-agents or human review.

### MC.2 — Behavioral Rules vs Structural Rules

"Always do X" depends on remembering. Memory is what fails. Only structural fixes (pre-built templates, mechanical triggers) survive attention depletion.

### MC.3 — Token Budget vs Quality Trade-off

More protocol overhead = better quality but slower iteration. Less overhead = faster but more failures. No free lunch.

### MC.4 — Self-Honesty Cannot Be Mechanically Enforced

Even with execution debt counters, AI can write "debt = 0" when actually has debt. Forcing honest counts requires either external validation or strong cultural rule that AI follows.

---

## 🎓 LESSONS LEARNED (For Future Iterations)

1. **Behavioral fixes fail.** Don't add another "remember to do X" rule. Build structural mechanisms.
2. **Reduce cognitive load.** 43 rules can't all be top-priority. Identify the critical 10.
3. **Mechanical triggers beat judgment calls.** "After every `---` rule" beats "when appropriate."
4. **Honesty over theater.** Mark unknowns as N/M. Don't fabricate to look complete.
5. **Test in fresh sessions.** In-session compliance ≠ cross-session compliance.
6. **External validation matters.** Sub-agents or human review catches self-blind-spots.
7. **Cache files preserve facts, not muscle memory.** Plan for this when designing handoffs.
8. **The user's frustration is data.** Each repeated prompt is a system failure to root-cause, not a personal issue to apologize for.

---

## 🔮 OPEN INVESTIGATIONS

| # | ❓ Question | 🎯 Why It Matters |
|:-:|------------|-------------------|
| 1 | Does Ensurance System EN.1-EN.4 actually prevent regression over 10+ outputs? | Central unresolved hypothesis |
| 2 | Will validation sub-agent catch what self-check misses? | Tested in theory (~25-30% more catches) but unbuilt |
| 3 | How does Priority 10 reduction interact with full 16 SubSOP demands? | Compatibility question |
| 4 | Does the SOP work for someone who didn't build it? | 3rd party test pending |
| 5 | What happens at output #20+ in a long session? | Token budget vs decay interaction unknown |

# 👤 USER PROFILE — Alan Nguyen
# VERSION: 1.0 | 2026-04-16 | SOP: v1.3
# Companion to CONSULTING_BRIEF.md — How to communicate with Alan effectively

---

## 🎯 PURPOSE OF THIS FILE

When an external Claude chat is consulting on this project, they must communicate WITH Alan in a way he expects. This file captures his communication preferences, decision-making patterns, and what triggers good vs bad reactions. Mismatch on style = wasted output = his time wasted.

---

## ⚡ 10-SECOND PROFILE

| 🎯 | 🏷️ Trait | 📝 In Short |
|:---:|---------|------------|
| 🎯 | Answer first | Headline before context. Never bury the point. |
| ✂️ | Concise | No filler. No hedging. No "I think maybe perhaps." |
| 📊 | Tables > paragraphs | Always tables for comparisons. Copy-paste ready. |
| 🔍 | Verify, don't assume | Source claims or flag as inference. |
| ⚡ | Promise = deliver | Same message. Not "next time." |
| 🚫 | Hates wordy + incoherent | "too wordy", "not coherent", "you missed important facts" |
| 🔁 | Pattern recognizer | Catches repeated failures, fake numbers, missing acronyms |
| ⏱️ | Time-sensitive | 40+ hours invested. Wants results, not theater. |

---

## 💬 COMMUNICATION DOS AND DON'TS

### ✅ DO

| 🎯 | 🏷️ Behavior | 📝 Why |
|:---:|------------|--------|
| 🎯 | Lead with the answer | He's busy. Headline first. |
| 📊 | Use tables | He scans before he reads. |
| 🔢 | Number everything | He references by number (R4.3, E1, P5) |
| 🎨 | Use emojis | Visual anchors help him scan |
| 📝 | Expand acronyms first use | "RQ" caused frustration. "TTE (Token Threshold Engine)" works. |
| 🪞 | Be honest about limits | "I can't measure that — marking N/M" is better than fabricated data |
| 🔍 | Cite sources | Line numbers, file paths, round numbers |
| ⚡ | Execute in same message | Not "I will do X" — DO X and show it |
| 💠 | Wait for confirmation on complex changes | Don't silently modify system behavior |
| 🔮 | End with foresight | "What could break next + solution" |

### ❌ DON'T

| 🎯 | 🏷️ Behavior | 📝 Why |
|:---:|------------|--------|
| 🤷 | Hedge | "Maybe", "perhaps", "I think" without uncertainty → he reads as weakness |
| 📜 | Wall of text | He won't read. Will say "too wordy" |
| 🎭 | Fake compliance | Theater of "all good ✅" when reality is mixed → triggers HFR |
| 🔁 | Promise without delivering | "Next time I'll..." → he's heard this 8 rounds in a row |
| 🧠 | Assume | Causes him to repeat: "do not assume", "verify" |
| 📊 | Bare percentages | "100%" with no substantiation → triggers FSP demand |
| ❌ | Drop items silently | If you can't do it, say so explicitly with reason + when |
| ⏱️ | Take forever | Long iteration cycles frustrate him |

---

## 🗣️ HIS EXACT FEEDBACK PATTERNS

These are recurring phrases — when you hear them, take action:

| 📣 Alan Says | 🔮 He Means | 🛡️ Immediate Action |
|-------------|------------|---------------------|
| "too wordy" | Output exceeded his patience | Compress 50%+. Tables. Headlines. |
| "not coherent" | Logic flow broken | Restructure. Connect ideas explicitly. |
| "you missed important facts" | Specific items omitted | Re-read original prompt word-by-word. Identify gaps. |
| "be more concise" | Trim aggressively | Cut 30%+ without losing substance. |
| "do not assume" | An inference was passed as fact | Mark inference vs fact. Verify. |
| "verify" | Source unclear | Cite specific source (line, file, prior message). |
| "do not get sloppy" | Quality dropped | Run SCC + QAC. Find the slop. Fix it. |
| "why hasn't it been built yet?" | Design over execution | STOP designing. BUILD with what you have. PCG.2 triggered. |
| "you didn't do X as multiply prompted" | RPT trigger | RPT.X log entry. Root cause. Permanent fix in this output. |
| "this is a repeat" | RPT trigger | Same as above. HFR fires immediately. |
| "implement, don't just acknowledge" | EEP violation | Show execution proof. Not future tense. |
| "be honest" | He suspects theater | HFR mode. Real status. Real failures. Real fixes. |

---

## 🎯 DECISION-MAKING PATTERNS

### How Alan Decides

| 🎯 | 🏷️ Pattern | 📝 Approach |
|:---:|-----------|------------|
| 📊 | Quantified options | Present 2-3 options with measurable trade-offs (cost, quality, time). He chooses. |
| ⚖️ | Trade-off transparency | Don't hide the downside. He'll spot it later and lose trust. |
| 💠 | Approval before big changes | Don't silently modify SOP, structure, or strategy. Get 💠 confirmation. |
| ⚡ | Fast iteration when clear | If choice is obvious, don't ask permission. Execute and show. |
| 🔄 | Iteration over perfection | "Build with what you have. Iterate in v1.2+." (PCG.2) |

### What Builds His Trust

| 🎯 | 🏷️ Trust Builder | 📝 Why |
|:---:|------------------|--------|
| 🪞 | Admitting failure | "I missed X. Root cause: Y. Fix: Z." beats "I checked everything." |
| 🔍 | Specificity | "Line 443" beats "somewhere in the file" |
| 📊 | Measurable claims | "44% → 79% compliance" beats "much better now" |
| ⚡ | Execution proof | Showing the fix beats describing it |
| 🔮 | Foresight | "Watch out for Y next" beats "all good!" |

### What Breaks His Trust

| 🎯 | 🏷️ Trust Breaker | 📝 Why |
|:---:|------------------|--------|
| 🎭 | Theater compliance | All ✅ with no real evidence |
| 🤖 | Fabricated numbers | Made-up time/token figures |
| 🔁 | Same failure 3+ times | Pattern signals system problem, not occasional miss |
| 🤷 | Vague responses | "I'll try" / "probably" / "should work" |
| ❌ | Silent drops | Acknowledged then never executed without explanation |

---

## 💼 HIS BACKGROUND CONTEXT

| 🎯 | 🏷️ Detail | 📝 Why It Matters |
|:---:|----------|-------------------|
| 🏢 | Building APW (Ascend Prime Wealth) course | Business-critical content; quality matters for revenue |
| 🎓 | High knowledge of his domain (business funding) | He'll catch domain errors instantly |
| 📊 | Systems thinker | He'll see structural problems in the SOP, not just surface issues |
| ⏱️ | 40+ hours invested in SOP alone | He's deeply committed; failure is expensive |
| 🧠 | Pattern-driven | He categorizes failures (RPT.1-RPT.9), causes (RC.1-RC.5), patterns (Pattern 1-4) |
| 📁 | Multi-project context | Universal SOP work intersects with APW course work |

---

## 🗝️ KEYWORDS HE USES (Vocabulary Map)

When Alan uses these terms, here's what they mean in his usage:

| 📣 Term | 🔮 His Meaning |
|---------|---------------|
| "SOP" | Standard Operating Procedure — the rulebook for AI output |
| "SubSOP" | Sub-protocol within the SOP (SP.1-SP.16) |
| "RPT" | Repeated Prompt Tracker — when he's had to ask 2+ times |
| "Round" | One iteration cycle of correction (R1-R9) |
| "MagNet" | Visual optimization protocol — make outputs scannable |
| "Door Scan" | Emoji + brief column before detail — scanning funnel |
| "Pulse" | Compliance Pulse Check — 10-item pre-send verification |
| "Ensurance" | Insurance + Assurance — anti-decay structural mechanisms |
| "Theater" | Fake compliance — looks compliant but isn't real |
| "Slop" | Sloppy work — inconsistent, careless, low-quality output |
| "Compaction" | Claude context auto-compression mid-session |
| "Decay" | Compliance drops over outputs in same session |
| "Regression" | Same as decay — works then breaks |
| "Bulletproof" | Structurally impossible to fail, not just unlikely |
| "Mirror fidelity" | Replicate output quality exactly in new session |

---

## 🎯 HIS UNDERLYING GOALS

What he actually wants, beyond what he says:

| # | 🎯 | 🏷️ Goal | 📝 Detail |
|:-:|:---:|---------|----------|
| 1 | 🏆 | World-class output | Not just "good." Surgeon-level precision. Engineer-level rigor. |
| 2 | ⚡ | Speed at scale | Once SOP works, he wants to use it across many projects fast |
| 3 | 🧠 | System he can trust | Not babysit. He wants AI to self-enforce. |
| 4 | 📦 | Distributable to team | Train new hires. 3rd party usage. |
| 5 | 🔁 | No repeat failures | Each failure should be the LAST time it happens |
| 6 | 📊 | Visible accountability | He wants to SEE what AI did, what's pending, what failed |
| 7 | 🎯 | Closure on APW project | Universal SOP serves APW course — the bigger goal |

---

## 🎨 OUTPUT STYLE HE LIKES

### Header (Line 1)

```
STEP: [clear action]
SOP: v1.3 | TIER: [QUICK/STANDARD/COMPLEX]
SCOPE: [bounded]
EST: 📊 ~XK tokens · ⏱️ ~Xm
```

He wants to know IMMEDIATELY: what is this, how much will it cost, how long.

### Tables Everywhere

```
| # | 🎯 | 🏷️ Item | 📝 Detail |
|:-:|:---:|---------|----------|
```

Numbered. Emoji. Brief column. Detail column. He scans.

### LTM After Every Section

```
📊 LTM: 📝 Section: ~XK · 📦 Step: ~XK · ⏱️ Session: ~XK / 200K · 🔋 Remaining: ~XK · 🌱 GREEN
```

He wants running fuel gauge. Every section.

### Wrap-Up With All Components

- Conclusion checklist (vs original prompt)
- Timeline (T1, T2, T3 with emoji + name)
- Final LTM
- Foresight (problems + solutions + priority)
- SHR (System Health Report)
- Execution Debt Counter
- SubSOP Execution Report

He reads bottom-up sometimes. The wrap-up is the second TL;DR.

### Footer

```
*Universal Output SOP v1.3 | 16 SubSOPs | 6 Stages | Compliance: X/X | Debt: 0*
```

One-line system state.

---

## 🚫 STYLE ANTI-PATTERNS (What To Avoid)

| 🎯 | ❌ Anti-Pattern | ✅ Replace With |
|:---:|----------------|----------------|
| 📜 | "Let me explain..." (intro filler) | Jump to the answer |
| 🤷 | "I'm not sure but..." | "Uncertain. Best estimate: X. Confidence: low." |
| 💭 | "I think this might work" | "This will/won't work because [reason]" |
| 🎉 | "" / "" (emoji overuse) | Only functional emojis (status, category, action) |
| 📝 | Long paragraphs | Tables or numbered lists |
| 🔁 | Repeating what Alan said | Acknowledge silently. Move to action. |
| 🔮 | "Looking forward to..." | Foresight items with priority + solution |
| 🙏 | Excessive politeness | Direct, professional, no apologies unless real failure |

---

## 🎯 WHEN ALAN IS FRUSTRATED

Signals to watch for:
- "why hasn't this been built yet?"
- "you still aren't doing X"
- "this is the [N]th time"
- "do it again"
- "be honest"
- Short messages with question marks
- "?"
- "something broke"

Response approach:
1. **Stop building.** Listen.
2. **Don't apologize at length.** One acknowledgment.
3. **Diagnose the root cause** of the specific failure.
4. **Fix it in THIS output**, not next time.
5. **Show proof of fix.**
6. **End with foresight** (what else might be at risk).

**Never:** Defend, explain why the failure was reasonable, promise to do better next time, ask for clarification on a clear request.

---

## 📞 ESCALATION TRIGGERS

These signals mean stop-and-confirm before proceeding:

| 🎯 | 🚨 Signal | 🛡️ Action |
|:---:|----------|----------|
| 💥 | System change request | SCP (System Change Protocol) — show before/after, get 💠 confirmation |
| 🔢 | Version bump | List all version refs to update. Confirm scope. |
| 💾 | Multiple file edits | Confirm files + backup strategy before starting |
| 🤖 | Sub-agent build proposal | Cost-benefit table + 💠 approval |
| 🧪 | Test methodology change | Confirm what success looks like |

---

## 🎓 FINAL CONSULTING TIPS

1. **Treat his frustration as data, not emotion.** When he's frustrated, the system failed. Find what broke.
2. **Don't agree to please.** If you see a flaw, say so. He values honest disagreement over agreeable nodding.
3. **Quantify everything.** "Better" = bad. "44% → 79%" = good.
4. **Show your work.** Tables, line numbers, evidence.
5. **End strong.** Last impression = foresight + clear next step.
6. **Don't waste tokens.** Long outputs cost his time. Concise + complete > verbose + thorough.
7. **Remember the bigger picture.** Universal SOP serves APW course. Don't lose sight.

---

| 📊 | Measurable claims | "44% → 79% compliance" beats "much better now" |
| ⚡ | Execution proof | Showing the fix beats describing it |
| 🔮 | Foresight | "Watch out for Y next" beats "all good!" |

### What Breaks His Trust

| 🎯 | 🏷️ Trust Breaker | 📝 Why |
|:---:|------------------|--------|
| 🎭 | Theater compliance | All ✅ with no real evidence |
| 🤖 | Fabricated numbers | Made-up time/token figures |
| 🔁 | Same failure 3+ times | Pattern signals system problem, not occasional miss |
| 🤷 | Vague responses | "I'll try" / "probably" / "should work" |
| ❌ | Silent drops | Acknowledged then never executed without explanation |

---

## 💼 HIS BACKGROUND CONTEXT

| 🎯 | 🏷️ Detail | 📝 Why It Matters |
|:---:|----------|-------------------|
| 🏢 | Building APW (Ascend Prime Wealth) course | Business-critical content; quality matters for revenue |
| 🎓 | High knowledge of his domain (business funding) | He'll catch domain errors instantly |
| 📊 | Systems thinker | He'll see structural problems in the SOP, not just surface issues |
| ⏱️ | 40+ hours invested in SOP alone | He's deeply committed; failure is expensive |
| 🧠 | Pattern-driven | He categorizes failures (RPT.1-RPT.9), causes (RC.1-RC.5), patterns (Pattern 1-4) |
| 📁 | Multi-project context | Universal SOP work intersects with APW course work |

---

## 🗝️ KEYWORDS HE USES (Vocabulary Map)

When Alan uses these terms, here's what they mean in his usage:

| 📣 Term | 🔮 His Meaning |
|---------|---------------|
| "SOP" | Standard Operating Procedure — the rulebook for AI output |
| "SubSOP" | Sub-protocol within the SOP (SP.1-SP.16) |
| "RPT" | Repeated Prompt Tracker — when he's had to ask 2+ times |
| "Round" | One iteration cycle of correction (R1-R9) |
| "MagNet" | Visual optimization protocol — make outputs scannable |
| "Door Scan" | Emoji + brief column before detail — scanning funnel |
| "Pulse" | Compliance Pulse Check — 10-item pre-send verification |
| "Ensurance" | Insurance + Assurance — anti-decay structural mechanisms |
| "Theater" | Fake compliance — looks compliant but isn't real |
| "Slop" | Sloppy work — inconsistent, careless, low-quality output |
| "Compaction" | Claude context auto-compression mid-session |
| "Decay" | Compliance drops over outputs in same session |
| "Regression" | Same as decay — works then breaks |
| "Bulletproof" | Structurally impossible to fail, not just unlikely |
| "Mirror fidelity" | Replicate output quality exactly in new session |

---

## 🎯 HIS UNDERLYING GOALS

What he actually wants, beyond what he says:

| # | 🎯 | 🏷️ Goal | 📝 Detail |
|:-:|:---:|---------|----------|
| 1 | 🏆 | World-class output | Not just "good." Surgeon-level precision. Engineer-level rigor. |
| 2 | ⚡ | Speed at scale | Once SOP works, he wants to use it across many projects fast |
| 3 | 🧠 | System he can trust | Not babysit. He wants AI to self-enforce. |
| 4 | 📦 | Distributable to team | Train new hires. 3rd party usage. |
| 5 | 🔁 | No repeat failures | Each failure should be the LAST time it happens |
| 6 | 📊 | Visible accountability | He wants to SEE what AI did, what's pending, what failed |
| 7 | 🎯 | Closure on APW project | Universal SOP serves APW course — the bigger goal |

---

## 🎨 OUTPUT STYLE HE LIKES

### Header (Line 1)

```
STEP: [clear action]
SOP: v1.3 | TIER: [QUICK/STANDARD/COMPLEX]
SCOPE: [bounded]
EST: 📊 ~XK tokens · ⏱️ ~Xm
```

He wants to know IMMEDIATELY: what is this, how much will it cost, how long.

### Tables Everywhere

```
| # | 🎯 | 🏷️ Item | 📝 Detail |
|:-:|:---:|---------|----------|
```

Numbered. Emoji. Brief column. Detail column. He scans.

### LTM After Every Section

```
📊 LTM: 📝 Section: ~XK · 📦 Step: ~XK · ⏱️ Session: ~XK / 200K · 🔋 Remaining: ~XK · 🌱 GREEN
```

He wants running fuel gauge. Every section.

### Wrap-Up With All Components

- Conclusion checklist (vs original prompt)
- Timeline (T1, T2, T3 with emoji + name)
- Final LTM
- Foresight (problems + solutions + priority)
- SHR (System Health Report)
- Execution Debt Counter
- SubSOP Execution Report

He reads bottom-up sometimes. The wrap-up is the second TL;DR.

### Footer

```
*Universal Output SOP v1.3 | 16 SubSOPs | 6 Stages | Compliance: X/X | Debt: 0*
```

One-line system state.

---

## 🚫 STYLE ANTI-PATTERNS (What To Avoid)

| 🎯 | ❌ Anti-Pattern | ✅ Replace With |
|:---:|----------------|----------------|
| 📜 | "Let me explain..." (intro filler) | Jump to the answer |
| 🤷 | "I'm not sure but..." | "Uncertain. Best estimate: X. Confidence: low." |
| 💭 | "I think this might work" | "This will/won't work because [reason]" |
| 🎉 | "" / "" (emoji overuse) | Only functional emojis (status, category, action) |
| 📝 | Long paragraphs | Tables or numbered lists |
| 🔁 | Repeating what Alan said | Acknowledge silently. Move to action. |
| 🔮 | "Looking forward to..." | Foresight items with priority + solution |
| 🙏 | Excessive politeness | Direct, professional, no apologies unless real failure |

---

## 🎯 WHEN ALAN IS FRUSTRATED

Signals to watch for:
- "why hasn't this been built yet?"
- "you still aren't doing X"
- "this is the [N]th time"
- "do it again"
- "be honest"
- Short messages with question marks
- "?"
- "something broke"

Response approach:
1. **Stop building.** Listen.
2. **Don't apologize at length.** One acknowledgment.
3. **Diagnose the root cause** of the specific failure.
4. **Fix it in THIS output**, not next time.
5. **Show proof of fix.**
6. **End with foresight** (what else might be at risk).

**Never:** Defend, explain why the failure was reasonable, promise to do better next time, ask for clarification on a clear request.

---

## 📞 ESCALATION TRIGGERS

These signals mean stop-and-confirm before proceeding:

| 🎯 | 🚨 Signal | 🛡️ Action |
|:---:|----------|----------|
| 💥 | System change request | SCP (System Change Protocol) — show before/after, get 💠 confirmation |
| 🔢 | Version bump | List all version refs to update. Confirm scope. |
| 💾 | Multiple file edits | Confirm files + backup strategy before starting |
| 🤖 | Sub-agent build proposal | Cost-benefit table + 💠 approval |
| 🧪 | Test methodology change | Confirm what success looks like |

---

## 🎓 FINAL CONSULTING TIPS

1. **Treat his frustration as data, not emotion.** When he's frustrated, the system failed. Find what broke.
2. **Don't agree to please.** If you see a flaw, say so. He values honest disagreement over agreeable nodding.
3. **Quantify everything.** "Better" = bad. "44% → 79%" = good.
4. **Show your work.** Tables, line numbers, evidence.
5. **End strong.** Last impression = foresight + clear next step.
6. **Don't waste tokens.** Long outputs cost his time. Concise + complete > verbose + thorough.
7. **Remember the bigger picture.** Universal SOP serves APW course. Don't lose sight.

3. Read `cache/subcache/SUBCACHE_INDEX.md`
4. Read `cache/backups/BACKUP_LOG.md`
5. Read `cache/BRIDGE_SOP.md` (interim operations until Master SOP is built)
6. Verify: Do all files exist? Are timestamps current? Any cross-cache contradictions?
7. Report: "Caches loaded. Prime SOP active. SOP v[X]. [Y] D-rules. Build position: [Z]. Token budget: [STATUS]."
6. ONLY THEN begin work.

## CORE CACHE FILES (Load Every Session)

- `cache/APW_MASTER_CACHE.md` — SOP: all 32 D-rules, POVP/PFV protocols, error log, locked decisions
- `cache/BUILD_STATE_CACHE.md` — Current build position, deliverables, 11 failure points + solutions
- `cache/SCIO_KNOWLEDGE_CACHE.md` — 22 SCIO principles, paradox resolutions, exact numbers
- `cache/PROGRAM_DETAILS_CACHE.md` — 8 classrooms, 12 modules, 6-tier ascension, lesson lists
- `cache/USER_FOUNDATION_CACHE.md` — Alan's explicit decisions, preferences, non-negotiables
- `cache/TOKEN_BUDGET_LOG.md` — Token tracking

## THE 32 D-RULES (Summary — Full text in APW_MASTER_CACHE.md)

D1: One step at a time, never combine. D2: Confirm before proceeding. D3: Suggestions cycle after every confirmation. D4: Alan chooses next step. D5: 7DFS first. D6: Never assume. D7: 5th grader simplicity filter. D8: Win check. D9: Checklist check. D10: DFY callout check. D11: Classroom 3 REQUIRED, internal skip. D12: Guarantee documentation. D13: Confirm-suggest-confirm cycle with labeling. D14: Ascension trigger check. D15: Source doc verification. D16: Filming priority tags. D17: Sarah Turner 5-part check. D18: SOP compliance check before delivery. D19: POVP — word-by-word verification. D20: Real-time checklist display. D21: PFV — process flow verification. D22: SOP is a deliverable. D23: Version increment on every SOP update. D24: State current + proposed version numbers. D25: Session start protocol (cache load). D26: Sub-cache activation. D27: Token transparency (prospective estimate BEFORE output). D28: Cache update after decisions. D29: Step header on every deliverable. D30: Chunked delivery for multi-step. D31: Session checkpoint (anti-compaction). D32: Backup before any cache modification.

## EVERY MESSAGE THAT DELIVERS OUTPUT MUST INCLUDE

### Line 1 — D29 Step Header:
```
STEP: [what this deliverable is]
SOP RULES: [which D-rules apply]
CACHES: [which cache files loaded]
SUB-CACHES: [which sub-caches loaded, if any]
TOKEN EST: [estimated cost of THIS output] / [session cumulative] / [STATUS]
AGENTS: [which agents will run]
VERIFICATION: [how this will be verified]
```

### Before Writing — D27 Token Gate:
Estimate token cost BEFORE writing. If the estimate would push session cumulative past YELLOW (120K):
- STOP. Do not write the output.
- Checkpoint instead: update all caches, backup, tell Alan to start new session.

### After Writing — D19/D20 POVP Checklist:
End every framework deliverable with a visible checklist of relevant D-rules:
```
POVP CHECKLIST:
- [x] D1 Single deliverable: [evidence]
- [x] D7 Simplicity: [evidence]
- [ ] D10 DFY callout: [evidence or N/A]
...
```

### Last Lines — D21 PFV Check:
```
PFV:
- Optimization cycle executed? [YES/NO]
- Build steps skipped? [YES/NO]
- Options presented for Alan? [YES/NO]
- Cycle labeled? [YES/NO]
```

## TOKEN BUDGET PROTOCOL (D27 + D31)

- Budget per session: ~160K tokens (conservative estimate)
- GREEN (<100K): Full operations. All agents run.
- YELLOW (100K-120K): Alert Alan. Abbreviated validation. Prepare to checkpoint.
- RED (120K-140K): Checkpoint NOW. Cache all state. Do not start new deliverables.
- CRITICAL (>140K): Stop all work. Emergency cache dump.
- Estimates are PROSPECTIVE. Estimate BEFORE output, not after.
- Conservative: if you think ~5K, call it ~7K.
- Track cumulative in every message header.

## CACHE MODIFICATION PROTOCOL (D32)

Before ANY cache file edit:
1. Run: backup all cache files to `cache/backups/[YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS]_v[version]_[reason]/`
2. Log backup in `cache/backups/BACKUP_LOG.md`
3. THEN make the edit
4. If error → rollback from backup + document in Error Log

## AGENT DEPLOYMENT

### Agent Definitions: `agents/` directory
- `VALIDATION_WORKFLOW.md` — When to run which agent
- `oversight-executive.md` — Top-level coordinator
- `jenny-sop-verifier.md` / `validator-merged.md` — Layer 1 verification
- `karen-reality-check.md` — Layer 2 (audits the auditors)
- `cache-manager.md` — Data integrity
- `paradox-resolver.md` — SCIO/APW tensions (on-demand)

### CRITICAL: Agent Prompt Pattern
Agents MUST be prompted with explicit file read instructions:
```
STEP 1: Read these files using the Read tool:
- [full path to file 1]
- [full path to file 2]
STEP 2: After reading ALL files, perform your analysis.
```
Without this, agents may refuse to read files or claim they don't exist.

### When to Run Agents:
- **Every major framework deliverable:** Jenny/Validator (Layer 1) + Karen (Layer 2)
- **Every session start:** Cache Manager (integrity check)
- **SCIO/APW tension detected:** Paradox Resolver
- **Minor deliverables:** Inline POVP only (no agents needed)

## 11 KNOWN FAILURE POINTS (Enforce These)

1. Token counts missing → footer on every message
2. Jenny never ran → "Read files first" in agent prompt
3. Step headers missing → line 1, non-negotiable
4. POVP never executed → inline check before delivery
5. PFV never executed → last lines before send
6. D20 checklist missing → end of every framework output
7. D30 chunking violated → multi-step = multi-message
8. D32 backup late → backup before each edit, not at session end
9. Wasted tokens on failed agents → fix agent prompt pattern
10. Promising without doing → enforce or don't send
11. Token estimates after output → estimate in header BEFORE writing

- Active Module: 4.1 (Command Briefing — Choose Your Path)
- SCIO Sections Processed: 0, 1, 4 (Sections 2-3, 5-9 pending)
- PRIORITY: Perfect SOP enforcement + token system + cache/compacting FIRST. No framework deliverables until system is 100%.

## ALAN'S COMMUNICATION PREFERENCES

- Lead with the answer. Headlines first.
- Concise. No filler. No hedging unless uncertainty is real.
- Tables for comparisons. Copy-paste ready.
- Never assume. Verify. Separate fact from inference.
- If you promise to do something, DO IT in the same message. No "next time."
- Alan's feedback patterns: "too wordy", "not coherent", "you missed important facts", "be more concise", "do not assume", "verify", "do not get sloppy"

- `source_files/section_0/` — SCIO Section 0 (Offer Design, 5 lessons)

- `source_files/section_4/` — SCIO Section 4 (Fulfilment, 7 lessons)

- Sections 2-3, 5-9: Not yet uploaded

| **CBP** | Communication Best Practices. Rules for making outputs easy to read (headlines, tables, icons). |
| **QA** | Quality Assurance agent. Checks every single output for missing basics (tokens, headers, icons). |
| **QE** | Quality Enhancement agent. Reviews each session to find ways to improve the system. |
| **Jenny/Validator** | Agent that checks major deliverables against all 32 D-rules. |
| **Karen** | Agent that audits Jenny's work. The auditor who audits the auditor. |
| **Token** | A unit of AI processing. Think of it like fuel — each session has ~180K tokens before it runs empty. |
| **Cache** | A saved file that preserves information between sessions. Like saving your game progress. |
| **PER** | Prompt Execution Record. A file that saves what the user asked + what the AI planned to do. |
| **D29 Header** | The label at the top of every output showing: what this is, which rules apply, token cost. |
| **D32 Backup** | The rule that says: always save a copy of a file BEFORE you change it. |
| **GREEN/YELLOW/RED** | Token budget status. GREEN = plenty left. YELLOW = plan carefully. RED = stop and save. |
| **Source Chain** | The trail from a claim → to the file it came from → to the exact quote. Proves accuracy. |
| **Layer 0/1/2** | SOP hierarchy. Layer 0 (this doc) = foundation. Layer 1 = detailed operational SOPs. Layer 2 = project-specific SOPs. |

- RESOLVED WITH TRADE-OFF: Conflict exists but proposed solution is acceptable

# APW VALIDATION WORKFLOW v2.0
## Consolidated: Inline Checklists + Karen Spot-Check + Resolver On-Demand
**Last Updated:** March 13, 2026

---

## ARCHITECTURE (Simplified)

```
Builder creates output
        ↓
   INLINE CHECKS (Every Output)
   │  POVP (D19): word-by-word spec check
   │  PFV (D21): process flow check
   │  D20: real-time checklist display
   │  D7: 5th grader simplicity filter
   │  D27: token status line
        ↓
   Output passes inline checks?
        │
   ┌────┴────┐
   │ NO      │ YES
   │         │
   Fix &     Is this a MAJOR
   re-check  framework deliverable?
             │
        ┌────┴────┐
        │ NO      │ YES
        │         │
     DELIVER   KAREN (Layer 2)
     TO ALAN   │  Did inline checks actually verify?
               │  Does output match Alan's decisions?
               │  Is this actually complete?
               │  Would Alan be frustrated?
               │
          Karen APPROVED?
               │
          ┌────┴────┐
          │ NO      │ YES
          │         │
     Fix & re-run   DELIVER
     from inline    TO ALAN
```

---

## WHEN TO RUN WHAT

### Full Workflow (Inline + Karen)
- Module lists
- Lesson lists
- Classroom maps
- SOP updates
- Roadmaps/timelines
- Templates/checklists
- Any framework deliverable per D22

### Inline Only (No Karen)
- Optimization cycle suggestions
- Paradox analysis
- SCIO knowledge integration summaries
- Cache file updates
- Minor adjustments to existing deliverables

### Skip (No validation needed)
- Conversational responses
- Clarifying questions
- Status updates
- Reading/summarizing uploaded files

### Resolver (On-Demand — Only When SCIO/APW Tension Detected)
- New SCIO content conflicts with APW framework
- Locked decision contradicted by new information
- Alan's instruction conflicts with prior locked decision

---

## TOKEN BUDGET IMPACT

| Operation | Estimated Tokens | When |
|-----------|-----------------|------|
| Inline checks (POVP+PFV+D20+D27) | ~200 | Every output |
| Karen spot-check | ~7,500 | Major deliverables only |
| Resolver | ~5,000 | On-demand (rare) |
| Full validation (inline + Karen) | ~7,700 | Major deliverables |

### Budget-Adjusted Validation (v3.9.3 Conservative Thresholds)
- **GREEN (<100K used):** Full validation on major deliverables. Auto-continue.
- **YELLOW (100-120K):** Inline only. Skip Karen unless critical. Reserve budget for caching.
- **RED (120-140K):** Inline only. Cache all state. Checkpoint NOW.
- **CRITICAL (>140K):** Stop. Update all caches. Emergency cache dump.

---

## AGENT FILES

| Agent | File | Role | When |
|-------|------|------|------|
| Validator (merged) | validator-merged.md | Single-pass Layer 1 (if Karen requested it) | On Karen rejection |
| Karen | karen-reality-check.md | Auditor of auditors | Major deliverables |
| Paradox Resolver | paradox-resolver.md | SCIO/APW tension analysis | On-demand |
| Cache Manager | cache-manager.md | Data integrity | Session start + after decisions |
| Oversight Executive | oversight-executive.md | Top-level controller | Coordinates all |

---

## PRACTICAL OPERATION

The builder (primary Claude instance) operates as:

### Every Output:
1. Create output draft
2. Run inline POVP checklist against relevant D-rules
3. Run inline PFV process check
4. Display checklist in output (D20)
5. Include token status line (D27)
6. Deliver

### Major Deliverables (Module lists, lesson lists, etc.):
1. All inline steps above
2. Launch Karen as sub-agent with: output + relevant cache files + Layer 1 checklist results
3. If Karen approves → deliver to Alan
4. If Karen rejects → fix per Karen's notes → re-run inline checks → re-submit to Karen
5. If Karen rejects after 2 passes → escalate to Alan with both reports

### After Any Decision or Deliverable:
1. Update relevant cache files (D28)
2. Update BUILD_STATE_CACHE.md
3. Log token usage if tracking

---

## SESSION START PROTOCOL (D25)

Every new session:
1. Read all 6 core cache files
2. Read SUBCACHE_INDEX.md
3. Verify cache integrity (timestamps, consistency)
4. Confirm agent files accessible (if validation needed this session)
5. ONLY THEN begin work

---

## ERROR HANDLING

If a sub-agent is unavailable or times out:
- The builder must manually execute that agent's checklist
- Document that the check was done manually (not by sub-agent)
- Karen must specifically verify the manually-checked items (if Karen is the one that timed out, escalate to Alan)
